newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIAN SEMIS - REMAIN ON THE OFFERED SIDE.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN SEMIS - REMAIN ON THE OFFERED SIDE.

text.p: *Semis retained their recent offered tone against the backdrop of a weakening Australian Treasury bond market, and yield spreads between the two markets continued to widen.
Semi-government bonds retained their recent offered tone against the backdrop of a weakening Australian Treasury bond market, and yield spreads between the two markets continued to widen.

Australian debt markets extended the sell-off seen late last week as fears of a strengthening U.S. economy gripped U.S. Treasuries, taking local long-dated yields to their highest level in around a month.
The semis markets continues to correct the strong rally seen earlier this year and is reversing the spread narrowing seen then, traders said.

"Semis are still offered as people still have a lot of stock on their books. The tax ruling last week added to the negative tone, but S&P came out and said it will not have an impact, and I guess that's what matters," one trader said.

The Australian High Court upheld a challenge against the rights of the states and territories to levy excise duties and in effect rendered franchise fees levied by state governments on tobacco, alcohol, and petrol constitutionally invalid.
Standard & Poor's said the decision would have no immediate impact on the ratings of any Australian states and territories.
These fees contributed A$5 billion of revenue to the states and territories in 1996 out of total state taxation of A$30.4 billion and total state government revenues of A$74.8 billion.
However, S&P said its view was based on the Australian government implementing a package of tax measures to offset the impact on state finances of losing the revenue sources.

"In the medium term, the change in the taxation arrangement for tobacco, alcohol, and petrol could have a small to negative influence on the ratings of the Australian states, but at this point this would not be sufficient to lead to a change in the rating of any particular state," the ratings agency said.

Meanwhile, as local economic data is fairly light this week, the direction of the domestic debt market is likely to come from the U.S. where there is a string of key indicators, not least July CPI, PPI and retail sales.
